newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds prices ended down 1/8 to 1/4 point Friday as a fading U.S. Treasury market and concern that munis have grown too "toppy" erroded morning strength.

"It's off 1/4 from yesterday, off 1/2 from the highs of this morning," one trader said. "Guys are starting to get fearful. I mean the last time we were down around this level we backed up to a 7.10 (percent yield) pretty quickly."
The municipal market saw a healthy amount of bonds out for the bid this week, and, though many bonds found permanent homes, players fear the market has gotten "a little toppy again," he said.

"Things are looking a little rich here. I mean munis are down around 82 percent of governments in terms of the insured side, and you know that's pretty much the lowest most guys feel we can go," the trader said. "So until we get the next break, whether it be up or down, guys are pretty much sitting on the sidelines."

A municipal analyst said prices were quoted down 1/8 point overall by late Friday. Prices opened 1/8 to 1/4 point higher, but began fading with Treasuries to be just 1/8 point higher by noon. The high-grade sector ended unchanged, while dollar bonds were quoted down 1/8 in line with the broader market, he said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 8/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed down 13/32 at 114-4/32. The December T-bond contract was down 11/32 at 109-15/32. The MOB spread was 149 ticks.

As for new issues, Bear Stearns & Co repriced and restructured $160.9 million California Public Works Board bonds, adjusting yields in some maturities. The deal featured a top yield of 5.82 percent in 2015.
Looking ahead, next week's scheduled competitive and negotiated issues are expected to number 95 and total $3.466 billion, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Fifty competitive sales totaling $1.598 billion are expected, with the largest a $168 million District of Columbia deal on October 3. Monday's biggest competitive issue is a $22.515 million New Hope-Solebury School District, Pa., sale scheduled for 1130 EDT.
Negotiated sales are expected to total $1.868 billion in 45 offerings. The largest deal is a $270 million Denver City & County Airport revenue bond offering via Lehman Brothers.
